original_test_intent: Verify for every required E1.S bay that actual approved read/write traffic reaches the correctly mapped NVMe and causes its activity indicator to flicker green, without data, media, controller, backplane or platform errors.
original_method: Select the unique row; map chassis/backplane bay, controller, namespace and drive serial/model/firmware; determine safe insertion and I/O policy; baseline device health, mounts and preserved logs; prove a disposable namespace or bounded file target and approve FIO direction, engine, block size, depth, jobs, runtime and verification; qualified operator inserts once; run the approved workload while timestamped video shows the correct bay changing from powered steady state to green activity flicker; correlate FIO IOPS/bytes/timestamps with the visual interval; stop on wrong target, data risk, media error, reset or abnormal LED and restore the approved state.
manual_activity: A qualified operator performs the approved insertion and continuously observes/records the correct bay LED while the approved FIO traffic runs; the owner confirms the target and destructive scope.
required_inputs: Chassis/backplane revision and bay-slot-controller to drive serial/model/firmware/namespace map
Disposable namespace or bounded file target with backup and active-stack exclusions
Exact FIO filename/device, read/write mix, ioengine, block size, depth/jobs, size/runtime and verification/cleanup
Authoritative green-flicker pattern, cadence/visibility and all-bay population scope
safety_requirements: Never infer a block device from numbering; prove serial/NGUID/EUI/UUID and exclude OS, boot, mounted, swap, LVM, RAID and unknown targets
Require explicit approval for any write and protect data with disposable media or bounded file scope
Use ESD and verified hot-plug/power procedure; do not force insertion
Preserve logs and collect pre/post SMART/NVMe error state
Abort on wrong target, unexpected mount/stack, I/O/media error, reset/disappearance, thermal fault, physical anomaly or incorrect LED; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate composite storage identity, active-stack exclusions, FIO recipe, approval and recovery
Collect read-only inventory/health and complete FIO stdout/stderr/exit/metrics after separate execution confirmation
Correlate timestamps with operator video without claiming visual observation
Do not select a device, write an unapproved target, insert hardware, infer LED from I/O, clear logs, retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve bay/drive/namespace map, destructive scope and exact FIO workload
Approve activity-LED visual oracle, population coverage and final storage state
Review correlated I/O/visual/health evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsblk` and `nvme list` are prechecks only. They do not run FIO, distinguish reads from writes or observe activity LED flicker; sshpass and host-key bypass are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run only the approved FIO job against the proven disposable namespace or bounded file target while the operator records the mapped bay LED, then collect complete job and health evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The insertion, FIO read/write activity, green-flicker criterion and 10/10-minute estimate remain; all workload and target parameters are pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Synchronize bounded approved FIO traffic metrics with timestamped direct activity-LED video and exact bay/serial/namespace identity for every required bay.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target safety, repeatable workload geometry, I/O-to-LED time correlation, health evidence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Enumeration, steady green power LED or uncorrelated flicker cannot prove the specified read/write activity indication.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Write workloads can destroy data and consume endurance; a cached workload or wrong namespace may produce misleading LED behavior, and visual cadence varies by firmware aggregation.

project_override_considerations: Engineering must decide whether the source requires destructive raw-device FIO or permits a bounded file workload, and whether read and write directions must be separately observed. `All E1.s` needs an explicit population matrix.
expected_evidence: Backplane/bay/controller/drive/namespace map plus safe insertion approval
Disposable/bounded target proof, active-stack exclusions, backup and exact FIO job file/hash
Complete FIO stdout/stderr/exit, bytes/IOPS/latency and timestamps for approved directions
Per-bay video/photo proving green flicker synchronized with I/O and correct drive identity
Pre/post NVMe health/error, preserved dmesg/journal/BMC/SEL/AER, cleanup/recovery and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requires FIO read/write plus physical green activity flicker. DeepSeek's enumeration-only result is an incomplete review, not a source-identity conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The activity-LED purpose is clear. Exact target, FIO recipe, bay map and visual specification are supplyable prerequisites, so execution remains gated rather than intrinsically blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2215 Wistron-HW-00490-V002: approve the chassis/backplane and complete bay/slot/controller-to-drive serial/model/firmware/namespace matrix, meaning of 'All E1.s', hot-plug/ESD procedure, disposable raw namespace versus bounded file target and active-stack exclusions, exact FIO read/write mix/ioengine/block size/depth/jobs/size/runtime/verify, green-flicker cadence/visibility oracle, abort limits, cleanup/final state and data/hardware recovery.

review_improvement: Restores both missing FIO and physical activity-LED coverage while preventing guessed targets, data loss, insecure access and uncorrelated visual claims.
independent_technical_reasoning: An activity LED must be causally correlated with I/O, not merely observed sometime after enumeration. FIO geometry changes request cadence and therefore apparent flicker, so direction, queueing, block size and runtime are part of the oracle. Raw-device writes are destructive and device names are unstable; serial/namespace identity plus active-stack exclusion is mandatory. Visual evidence remains manual, while FIO metrics and health logs are automatable, which makes this a hybrid confirmation-gated case rather than MANUAL ONLY.
